bib.title: Introduction to Machine Learning with Python, Chapter 3: Unsupervised Learning and Preprocessing

question: How do scalers, decomposition (PCA, NMF), manifold learning (t-SNE) and clustering (k-means, agglomerative, DBSCAN) transform and explore unlabeled data in scikit-learn, and how can their output be evaluated?
contributions: Walkthrough of preprocessing scalers and the fit/transform discipline
PCA, NMF, t-SNE on cancer, faces, digits and synthetic data
k-means, agglomerative and DBSCAN clustering with failure cases and evaluation (ARI, silhouette)

limits: Dated 2016 scikit-learn API: np.bool, fetch_lfw_people defaults, TSNE defaults (perplexity, init, learning rate) and KMeans n_init default have since changed; code needs updating before rerun.
Chapter's own errors: image shape given as 87x65 in In[22] but as 50x37 pixels in the PCA components text (components_ shape is (100, 5655), 87*65=5655).
In[26]-[28] first uses 1-NN accuracy from a single split, no repeats or variance; clustering numbers come from single runs.
Robustness-based clustering metrics are said to be not implemented in scikit-learn at the time of writing.
Numeric ARI (random, k-means, agglomerative) and silhouette scores for two_moons appear only in figure panel titles, not in text.
Silhouette is said to often not work well in practice; no other label-free metric is developed (no elbow, no gap statistic, no PCA explained variance ratio, no UMAP).
In[77] is labelled In[78] output (Out[78]) in the text: a numbering slip.
Sparse coding, ICA, factor analysis only pointed to, not covered.
practices: Fit scalers on the training set only and apply the same transform to the test set; never rescale the test set separately (p.136-138).
Use fit_transform on the training set; use scikit-learn's scalers rather than reimplementing them (p.138-139).
Scale features with StandardScaler before PCA (p.144).
Use whiten=True PCA before distance-based classifiers such as 1-NN (p.150).
Use RobustScaler when outliers distort mean and variance; Normalizer when only direction matters (p.133-134).
Use NMF for additive data (audio, gene expression, text); NMF needs non-negative features and a random_state (p.156, 161).
Use t-SNE only for exploratory 2-D visualisation; it has no transform for new data (p.164).
Scale data before choosing DBSCAN eps; eps matters more than min_samples (p.189-190).
Evaluate clustering with ARI or NMI, never accuracy, when ground truth exists (p.193).
Without ground truth, inspect clusters manually; silhouette favours compact clusters (p.193-195).
Beware DBSCAN label -1 when indexing arrays with cluster labels (p.190).
Use ward linkage by default; average or complete when cluster sizes are very unequal (p.182).
Use MiniBatchKMeans for very large datasets (p.181).

terms.definition: a method that rotates the dataset in a way such that the rotated features are statistically uncorrelated
components and coefficients are both required to be greater than or equal to zero
each point is represented using a single component, given by the cluster center
at least min_samples data points within a distance of eps of a point
measure of agreement between a clustering and ground truth clustering, 0 for random, 1 for identical (ignores label names)
rescales the principal components to have the same scale; same as StandardScaler after the transformation
trying to find the odd one out
agglomerative clustering where each intermediate step gives a clustering with a different number of clusters
